info.name: Nexmile — Merchant
info.description:
Everything a **merchant** can do over the API.

**Merchants sign in with a password, not an OTP** — unlike customers and riders. Registration happens on the website at `nexmile.in/merchants/register`; the API endpoint exists for completeness.

Restaurants use the web portal at `nexmile.in/merchants` today, so this collection is mainly for a future merchant app and for testing. Everything here has a portal equivalent.

**Update is POST, not PATCH, on menu items** — PHP does not parse multipart bodies on PATCH, so a PATCH upload arrives with an empty `$_FILES`.

Full reference: `docs/MENU_AND_ORDERS.md`

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description: Password-based. Registration is on the website, not in the app.

request.description: Creates the account as `pending`. In practice merchants register on `nexmile.in/merchants/register`.
`identifier` accepts the registered email **or** the 10-digit mobile number.
The signed-in merchant account.
Ends this session.

item.name: 2. Profile and storefront
item.description: What a customer sees, and whether the shop is open.

request.description: KYC fields are read-only here.

**Coordinates matter more than anything else here.** A merchant without them is invisible to every customer.

`commission_rate` is deliberately **not** settable — it is a contract term, changed only by Nexmile.
The most-used control a merchant has. Refuses to open with 403 until KYC is verified and the FSSAI licence is current.
Plus `is_open_now` and `within_operating_hours`.

**Replaces the whole week**, never merges — a partial write could leave the shop open on a day just closed. `day_of_week` is 0 Sunday to 6 Saturday; days omitted are closed.

A closing time earlier than the opening time means past midnight: 18:00–01:00 is open all evening.
multipart. JPG, PNG or WebP up to 4 MB. The logo is the first thing a customer sees.
Path segment is `logo` or `banner`.

item.name: 3. Verification (KYC)
item.description: FSSAI certificate, PAN and bank proof are required before a merchant can trade.

request.description: What is uploaded, what is missing, and whether it can be submitted.
multipart. JPG, PNG or PDF up to 10 MB.
Pending or rejected only.
Usually reviewed within two working days.

item.name: 4. Menu — categories
item.description: Deleting a category keeps its items and clears their grouping.

request.description: With item counts.
Inactive categories are hidden from customers.
Send only what changes.
Items survive and become uncategorised.
Filterable.
multipart so the photo goes with the item in one call. GST is restricted to statutory rates.
With its option groups.
**POST, not PATCH** — PHP does not parse multipart bodies on PATCH.
Its own endpoint because it is the one action performed mid-service, on a phone.
Leaves the item in place.
Soft delete — past orders keep resolving.
The whole ordered list in one call, so the menu cannot be left half-reordered.

item.name: 6. Menu — choices
item.description: "Spice level", "Add-ons", "Choose your rice". Without these half a menu cannot be expressed.

request.description: With their options.

**Options are sent with the group**, never separately — a group with no choices is a dead end at checkout.

Refused if a customer could never satisfy it: min above max, min above the number of choices, single-choice with max above 1, or required with min 0.
Sending `options` reconciles the list: entries with an `id` are updated in place, new ones created, anything absent removed. Keeping ids matters — historical order lines reference them.
Removes the group and its choices.
The kitchen runs out of paneer, not of the whole "choose your filling" group.

item.name: 7. Orders
item.description: Unpaid orders never appear — `pending_payment` is filtered out of every list.

request.description: Oldest first: the ticket waiting longest needs attention. `?history=1` for completed ones, newest first.
Items, options, customer, timeline and the pickup code.
Optional `prep_minutes` — without it the merchant's configured average is used, so the customer always gets an estimate.
Only before accepting. Reason required, minimum 10 characters — the customer reads it. No cancellation fee.
From `accepted`.
Puts a delivery order onto the rider board. The pickup code becomes visible at this point.
Different act from rejecting: the kitchen said yes and then something went wrong. Refused once a rider holds the order — at that point cancelling is a phone call.
